question: I am in Canada and bought the starter kit for 80 dollars; the stove's original share of the 100-dollar individual total was 50 dollars. At day 20 after delivery I want to return only the unused empty stove. What item refund applies, who arranges return shipping, and can I use the store's 7-dollar label?

searches.query: I am in Canada and bought the starter kit for 80 dollars; the stove's original share of the 100-dollar individual total was 50 dollars. At day 20 after delivery I want to return only the unused empty stove. What item refund applies, who arranges return shipping, and can I use the store's 7-dollar label?

chunks.text: Who pays for a return label  For ordinary domestic change-of-mind returns, the store offers a ground label for USD 7 per parcel. If the customer uses it, USD 7 is deducted from the refund or store credit. A customer may instead arrange and pay for their own suitable carrier. A store label covers one parcel; two parcels require two labels. Membership does not waive this fee.  An approved wrong-item shipment or manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid label without the USD 7 deduction. The support team must approve that reason first. A customer selecting a defect reason in the portal is not sufficient proof that the claim has been approved. The hiking boot fit trial is a fit return, so the normal USD 7 label fee applies unless the customer supplies their own shipping.  Use suitable packaging and keep the carrier acceptance receipt. Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service.

Camping fuel and stove returns  The online store sells empty camping stoves and accessories but does not ship filled fuel canisters. Fuel is sold for store collection only where a store is authorized to stock it. A stove listing does not mean fuel is included. Customers should check the compatible fuel type in the product instructions before buying fuel separately.  Never include a used or full fuel canister in a stove return. Remove any fuel container before arranging an eligible stove return and follow the manufacturer's instructions for making the stove safe. If the stove has leaked or appears unsafe, contact support for the product-specific procedure instead of using an ordinary label.  An unused stove bought online follows the standard return policy unless it was marked final sale. A stove bought as part of the starter kit uses the discounted-bundle allocation for its paid item value. The allocation does not authorize sending fuel through the mail.

Refund allocation for discounted bundles  When a bundle has one discounted purchase price, allocate that price across its items in proportion to their individual prices at the time of purchase. Refunding one eligible item returns that allocated paid amount. It does not return the item's current price or its undiscounted original price. Retaining other items does not by itself cancel the allocation.  The camping starter kit contains a lantern listed at USD 30, a stove listed at USD 50, and a carry case listed at USD 20. Their individual prices total USD 100. When the customer paid USD 80 for the kit, the allocated paid amounts are USD 24 for the lantern, USD 40 for the stove, and USD 16 for the case. These amounts total the USD 80 actually paid.  The allocation determines money, not return eligibility. Check the condition, return window, gift status, and transport restrictions separately.

searches.query: return window policy days after delivery

chunks.text: Product return and warranty windows start from the recorded collection date for a pickup order. Other eligibility conditions, including final-sale markings and product-specific trials, still apply.

When refunds arrive  The returns team normally inspects an ordinary parcel within five business days after warehouse receipt. Once the return is approved, the store submits the refund within two business days. A bank-card provider may then take another three to five business days to show the credit. These stages happen in sequence. A carrier delivery notification is not the same event as a completed inspection.  For planning, the longest published path is five business days for inspection, two for submission, and five for the card provider: up to 12 business days after warehouse receipt. That is a policy estimate, not a live payment-status lookup. Weekends and published holidays do not count as business days. A missing component or a dispute over condition can require further review.  Gift recipients receiving store credit are sent that credit after approval. The three-to-five-day bank-card processing period does not apply to issuing store credit. This page does not identify whether a particular return has been received, approved, or refunded.

Reporting delivery damage or the wrong product  Report visible transport damage or a wrong product within seven calendar days after delivery. Keep the outer packaging and photograph the label, packing materials, and affected item. The support team compares those details with the shipment record before approving the claim. If the item is unsafe to use, stop using it while the report is assessed.  An approved wrong-product or delivery-damage return receives a prepaid label. The customer does not pay the ordinary USD 7 change-of-mind label fee for that approved return. The team confirms whether a replacement or another remedy will be provided. A report being opened does not prove replacement inventory exists or establish a delivery date for the replacement.  Damage involving a rechargeable battery follows the separate damaged-battery procedure. Do not put a leaking or swollen battery in an ordinary return parcel even when support is investigating delivery damage. A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process.

International deliveries and returns  The store ships eligible ordinary products to Canada and the United Kingdom. International standard shipping costs USD 22 per order. Domestic membership and ordinary free-delivery thresholds do not apply to international shipping. Local import taxes and customs charges are paid by the recipient and are separate from the amount charged by the store.  Lithium-battery products, kayaks, and rigid roof cargo boxes are excluded from international delivery. An item being small enough to fit in a parcel does not remove a lithium-battery restriction. An international customer must not select a domestic destination as a placeholder and expect support to reroute a restricted product across the border.  Eligible international change-of-mind returns use the normal unused-condition and return-window rules. The customer arranges and pays the return transport. The store does not issue the USD 7 domestic return label for an international parcel. Import taxes are not refunded by the store.

An international customer may use the return route if eligible and place a separate new order. Import taxes and international return transport are covered in the international-orders article. Exchange approval does not automatically waive a return-label fee.

Import taxes are not refunded by the store. Direct size or color exchanges are unavailable for international orders; return an eligible item and place a new order instead. Availability, exchange rates, and customs clearance times for a particular order are not maintained in these policy pages.

answer.answer: The item refund is USD 40. Calculation: The starter kit was purchased for USD 80, and the stove's individual price was USD 50 out of a USD 100 total. The allocated paid amount for the stove is (50/100) × 80 = USD 40. Because you are in Canada, you are an international customer and must arrange and pay for return shipping yourself. You cannot use the store's USD 7 label, as it is for domestic returns only.
